title: In 2 Chronicles 23 What Does This Chapter Teach Us About The Role Of Leadership In Relation To Gods Covenant
paragraphs: The Restoration of Covenant Leadership: Lessons from 2 Chronicles 23

2 Chronicles 23 is a dramatic account of restoration, courage, and covenant faithfulness. Set during a dark period in Judah’s history, this chapter chronicles the overthrow of the wicked queen Athaliah and the enthronement of the rightful king, Joash, under the guidance of the godly priest Jehoiada. It powerfully demonstrates the essential role of leadership in upholding God’s covenant and guiding God’s people.
1. The Importance of Righteous Leadership

At the heart of the narrative is Jehoiada, the high priest, who played a pivotal role in preserving the Davidic line and restoring covenant faithfulness. For six years, Joash was hidden in the temple, protected from Athaliah’s murderous intent (2 Chronicles 23:3 ASV). Jehoiada’s actions underscore that godly leadership is not passive but actively seeks to align the nation with God’s revealed will.

And all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said unto them, Behold, the king’s son shall reign, as Jehovah hath spoken concerning the sons of David. - 2 Chronicles 23:3 ASV

Here, leadership involves not just ruling but ensuring faithfulness to God’s promises. Jehoiada reminds the people of God’s covenant with David, emphasizing that true leadership upholds God’s Word, not human ambition.
2. Leadership’s Responsibility to Lead in Covenant Renewal

Jehoiada leads the people in renewing their covenant with God and with the king. This twofold covenant—vertical with God, horizontal with the king—demonstrates that biblical leadership is responsible to God first and then to the community.
And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, and all the people, and the king, that they should be Jehovah’s people. - 2 Chronicles 23:16 ASV
This public commitment calls the whole nation back to its identity as God’s people. Leaders, therefore, are to model and facilitate covenant renewal—calling people back to obedience and worship.
3. Zeal Against Idolatry

The chapter records the destruction of the temple of Baal and the removal of its priest (2 Chronicles 23:17 ASV). Godly leadership does not tolerate compromise with sin or idolatry but leads in repentance.
And all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. - 2 Chronicles 23:17 ASV
This act is significant: it shows that leadership must confront sin and cleanse the people from corrupt influences, leading them back to pure worship of the LORD.
4. Leadership’s Role in Worship and Order

Jehoiada reestablishes the proper roles for priests and Levites, ensuring that worship in the temple is conducted according to God’s law (2 Chronicles 23:18 ASV). True leadership is about more than authority—it is about stewardship and service, ensuring God’s commands are followed.

And Jehoiada appointed the officers of the house of Jehovah under the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David had distributed in the house of Jehovah... as it is written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, according to the order of David. - 2 Chronicles 23:18 ASV
Leaders are called to uphold the pattern of worship and order prescribed by God, not to invent their own ways.
5. The Blessing of Covenant-Faithful Leadership
The result of this godly leadership is joy, peace, and security for the people (2 Chronicles 23:21 ASV). The covenant restoration brings about God’s blessing upon the community.
So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. And Athaliah they had slain with the sword. - 2 Chronicles 23:21 ASV
Where godly leadership prevails, the fruit is spiritual renewal and the flourishing of God’s people.
New Testament Connections

The principles seen here echo in the New Testament, where Christ is the ultimate covenant leader—the Good Shepherd who faithfully fulfills God’s promises (John 10:11 ASV). Church leaders are called to shepherd God’s flock with integrity (1 Peter 5:2-3 ASV), always pointing to Christ and upholding the truth of the gospel (2 Timothy 2:15 ASV).
Conclusion

2 Chronicles 23 teaches that godly leadership is crucial for covenant faithfulness. Leaders are to remember God’s promises, lead in repentance and worship, guard against idolatry, and ensure that God’s Word is central. Ultimately, such leadership points to Jesus Christ, the perfect covenant King.
